claims.text: Controlled annealing at approximately 700°C for an extended duration promotes chemical short-range order in NiFeCoCrMn.
Rapid quenching retains a comparatively disordered NiFeCoCrMn state with minimal chemical short-range order.
Enhanced chemical short-range order produces heterogeneous local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions associated with chemical short-range order impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength in annealed NiFeCoCrMn.
Impeded dislocation motion increases strain hardening in annealed NiFeCoCrMn.
Chemical short-range order modifies local stress fields in a way that delays crack initiation.
Annealed samples with pronounced chemical short-range order will have higher yield strength than rapidly quenched, disordered samples.
Annealed samples with pronounced chemical short-range order will have greater strain-hardening rates than rapidly quenched, disordered samples.
Annealed samples with pronounced chemical short-range order will exhibit later crack initiation or delayed failure relative to rapidly quenched samples.
The predicted mechanical effects are attributable to chemical short-range order only if precipitation, grain growth, and other significant thermally induced microstructural changes are absent.
The proposed chemical-short-range-order mechanism should operate in NiFeCoCrMn from room temperature to approximately 400°C.
Atom probe tomography and TEM can confirm that the starting samples have a uniform, fully disordered microstructure.
In situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction and TEM can verify that annealing has not caused precipitation or grain growth.
A comparison of annealed and rapidly quenched samples with identical overall composition can isolate the effect of chemical short-range order when other microstructural changes are excluded.

Failure to obtain reproducibly higher yield strength and strain-hardening rates in samples with pronounced chemical short-range order would falsify the proposed dominant role of chemical short-range order.
An association between mechanical improvements and unintended precipitation or grain growth would falsify attribution of those improvements primarily to chemical short-range order.
